name: example -- the face in shot 1, frame by frame
note: Paths are relative to this file. The sample frames are not added to the repository: they are a measurement source, not our work.
before_note: the images of the file DELIVERED in the previous pass -- not a re-render from the old sources (a render also reads the files that changed later; METHOD 11)

anchor.name: near_eye
anchor.note: The anchor is measured on the SAMPLE; relative probes are computed from it. The gaps between sparse seeds are filled linearly. Do not use a feature whose shape changes (an eye, a place where tears gather) for the head TRACK -- take the track from rigid landmarks (an edge, the chin, the jaw).

probes.name: far_eye
probes.note: the core of the iris. At L<30 it joined the temple line above and pulled the centre up by 3 px -- threshold 22.

probes.name: chin_front_y52
probes.note: a rigid landmark: in the held images it must stay the same to within 0.1 px

probes.name: jaw_tear
probes.note: each frame its own box. 'brightest' takes the BRIGHTEST thing in the box -- if a snow particle is brighter than the ring's glint, it takes the particle. Keep the box tight and check the result on a sheet.

probes.name: hand_tip
probes.note: choose the threshold FAR from the background: at <26 the mask leaked into the sky of L 17..30 and the 'tip' was found on the edge of the box.

silhouettes.name: body_right
silhouettes.note: the right edge of the figure in every row. The seed -- the darkest spot of the body (if it lands on a particle, the largest component in the 9x9 window is taken).
